text: Code refactoring is the process of improving the structure of existing code without changing what it does. The main goal is to make the code easier to read, understand, and maintain. Developers often refactor to remove duplication, simplify complex logic, and give variables clearer names. Even though the behavior stays exactly the same, the quality of the code improves. Refactoring also helps reduce technical debt, which builds up when quick fixes and poor design decisions pile up over time. By refactoring regularly, teams keep their codebase healthy and make future changes faster and safer.
